title: 56th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting ran from 09:00 to 10:06. Two government bills (a Drugs Act amendment and a Vice President's Office bill) had their first reading, and the Speaker said an urgent matter from the South Galolhu member did not meet the rules to be tabled. The main business was debate on the Economic Committee's report on the bill amending the Copyright and Related Rights Act (23/2010), which lengthens protection from 50 to 70 years; PNC members and some others backed it, MDP members questioned how ministries were consulted, and the chair repeatedly asked speakers to stay on the report. The bill then passed 57 votes to none.

items.title: Announcements by the chair: urgent matter from South Galolhu member Meekail Ahmed Nasym
items.outcome: not tabled; did not meet conditions in Rule 197

items.title: First reading: bill to amend Law 17/2011 (Drugs Act), submitted by the government through the Gamu member Yoosuf Nasheed
First reading: Vice President's Office bill, submitted by the government through the South Maafannu member Abdulla Rifau
Economic Committee report on the bill to amend Law 23/2010 (Copyright and Related Rights Act), submitted by Nilandhoo member Fathimath Sauda
items.outcome: debated; 1 hour allotted (PNC 39 min, MDP 8, MDA 3, JP 3, MNP 3, others 2 each)

items.title: Third reading and vote on the Copyright and Related Rights Act amendment bill

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Linked the copyright debate to alleged misuse of state resources and a television channel; the chair repeatedly asked him to keep to the report.
Raised several points of order, including on how his speaking time was signalled and on remarks about interviews.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the amendments, saying they protect many rights and businesses.
Criticised the opposition MDP for not taking a responsible approach to the bill and raised past corruption allegations.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Supported the report; said the amendments help creators and open chances to market their work to tourism.
Challenged claims that ministries were not consulted, saying the bill was drafted with input and some ministries were created later.
Raised points of order that other speakers were straying from the bill.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Recalled how the bill was submitted and asked whether MDP had enough time to debate it.
Supported the bill's aim of securing rights, while criticising the opposition's remarks.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said ministries told the committee they had little information about the bill, and the committee gave them extra time.
Pointed to page 6 of the report listing the bodies the committee met; congratulated the Madifushi school volleyball team.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Said the old copyright law was outdated and the amendments bring Maldivian creators' rights in line with other countries.
Raised a point of order that a colleague's remarks concerned a separate matter, not the bill.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the amendments and thanked the Nilandhoo member for submitting the bill.
Gave the example of resort designs being copied; urged all members to pass the bill.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the bill had received ample time and consultation, and that the Majlis was working extra days into mid-December.
Raised a point of order that remarks were off the bill and against the Majlis rules.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Supported the report; said the committee consulted ministries, councils and individuals widely, and the bill protects artists and craftspeople.
Criticised the opposition's objections and said MDP had not raised concerns in committee.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Raised a point of order on the time allowed and on the record of ministries' comments in the committee.

speakers.name: Ali Fazad
positions: Presented the Economic Committee report: bill aligns copyright law with international conventions, adds exceptions, extends protection from 50 to 70 years, and asks the Majlis to pass it.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the amendments; said protecting creations encourages young creators, investment in talent and business growth.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Raised a point of order objecting to remarks about the ruling PNC government made by a colleague.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Said the bill protects artists' and workers' rights; objected to the tone of debate with students watching and urged members to keep to the report.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Said the debate should be on the committee's report and on protecting young creators; regretted the political tone.

decisions: The Speaker ruled that the South Galolhu member's urgent matter did not meet the conditions of Rule 197 and was not tabled.
Bill to amend Law 17/2011 (Drugs Act) and the Vice President's Office bill were read a first time.
The bill amending the Copyright and Related Rights Act (Law 23/2010) passed its third reading, 57 in favour, none against.
Next sitting set for Tuesday 3 December 2024 at 09:00.

votes.what: Passing the bill to amend the Copyright and Related Rights Act (Law 23/2010), per the Economic Committee report (58 present, 57 voted; 29 needed)
